newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate bond market sizzles with new deals.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate bond market sizzles with new deals.

text.p: The primary market continues to sizzle with activity as issuers capitalize on steady buyside demand to bring more deals, syndicate sources said.
"A calendar is certainly building, names continue to pop into the market," said one syndicate source.
Among new deals rumored to come to market are Chrysler Corp unit Chrysler Financial's $300 million five-year debt offering via Merrill Lynch & Salomon Brothers, sources said.
Price talk is seen in the +40 basis points area, sources added.
In addition, Banc One may also tap the primary market with a three-part $750 million debt offering, sources said.
The Banc One deal is expected to include the following tranches, syndicate sources added.
-$250 million of a three-year issue with price talk seen at +30 basis points over Treasuries,
-$250 million of a five-year issue with price talk seen at +40 basis points over Treasuries,
-$250 million of a seven-year issue with price talk seen at +50 basis points area, syndicate sources said.
Goldman Sachs & Co is expected to underwrite the offering, sources added.
Dealers said despite higher U.S. Treasury yields than a week ago, issuers are rushing to get their financing done now as the threat of higher interest rates looms over the market.
A week ago, the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond was quoted at 6.81 percent at the close. Currently, the U.S. T-bond is trading up 2/32 at 95-27/32 to yield 6.96 percent.
Next week the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), the policy-setting arm of the Federal Reserve Board, will meet to vote on U.S. monetary policy.
Also, on tap is a $200 million deal for Cooper Tire & Rubber Co, with a 30-year noncallable maturity, sources said. Merrill Lynch is expected to underwrite the deal.
Meanwhile, another $2.1 billion in private placement debt offerings are getting set to hit the market, dealers said.
Leading the way is Montell Polyolefins NV, which is expected to tap the U.S. market with a $750 million debt offering, sources said.
Montell NV is a 50/50 plastics joint venture between Royal Dutch/Shell and Italy's Montedison.
The deal, which is expected to price on Wednesday, includes $500 million in 10-year 144A notes and $250 million in 30-year 144A notes, sources said.
The offering is expected to be underwritten by Morgan Stanley & Co Inc.
Quest Communications is also expected to bring a $450 million two part 144A debt offering via Salomon Brothers.
The B2/B-plus rated deal consists of $200 million in 10-year senior notes and $250 million (proceeds) of 10-year senior discount notes.
Also, Borg-Warner Security Corp is expected to issue $125 million in 10-year 144A senior subordinated notes via Merrill Lynch & Co.
EV International is expected to set $100 million in 10-year 144A senior subordinated notes via Chase Securities.
Key Plastics Inc is expected to bring $125 million in B3/B-minus rated 144A senior subordinated notes due 2007 via Lehman Brothers.
Also, Prime Hospitality Corp is expected to tap the market with $200 million in B1/B-plus rated 144A senior subordinated notes due 2007 via Merrill Lynch & Co.
Spanish Broadcasting System Inc is also expected to issue a $250 million in two-part 144A debt offering via sole manager CIBC Wood Gundy.
The deal consist of $75 million in senior notes due 2004 and $175 million in senior exchange pik preferred securities.
STC Broadcasting Inc is also expected to issue $100 million in 10-year 144A senior subordinated notes via Chase Securities.
Among other high-yield offerings, Central Tractor Farm & Country is expected to issue $100 million in B1/B-plus rated senior notes due 2007 via Nationsbanc Capital markets, sources said.
Intercel Inc said it also planned to issue $300 million in senior notes due 2007 via Morgan Stanley & Co.

Another $150 million is expected to come from Titan Wheel International. The offering is expected to include a 10-year B1/BB-minus rated senior subordinated note issue and will be underwritten by Merrill Lynch & Co.
